summary: Temporal priority decay computation miscalibration causing stale SLA priorities
description:
Issue summary: The background 'temporal priority decay' job that lowers ticket routing priority over time is producing incorrect decay values across multiple templated routing cohorts. Impact: Tickets remain at high-priority longer than intended, causing skewed routing to SRE/Oncall and elevated workload in specific escalation cohorts. This also contaminates weekly SLA reports and inflates mean time to respond metrics.

Environment: Observed in prod-us-east and prod-eu-west. Affected subsystems: sla-service (decay calculator), routing-engine (priority application), template-compiler (cohort binding).

Observed behaviour: Decay curve values are ~3x slower than expected for tickets created after 2026-02-28 02:00 UTC; some cohorts show no decay for 12+ hours. Expected behaviour: Decay should follow configured half-life windows per-template (e.g., 6-hour half-life for P1->P2).

Initial detection: Weekly SLA report (2026-03-01) flagged a jump in P1 open-ticket median age; on-call flagged unusual manual escalations.

Why this is unique: Unlike previous routing-template drift tickets, this appears tied to timebase calculation and leader-election interactions causing double-application of timezone normalization logic for cohorts created near DST boundary and for templates created by the new template-authoring flow (template-compiler v2).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a test routing template with a temporal-priority-decay window: half_life_hours=6 and cohort tag=prod-escalation-test
2) Create several tickets with created_at timestamps near a DST/UTC boundary (e.g., 2026-02-28 01:30 UTC to 03:30 UTC), assign cohort tag
3) Observe decay job runs (scheduled every 10 minutes) and record computed priority at T+1h, T+3h, T+6h
4) Expect exponential decay per half-life; actual values show near-linear or no change for some cohorts
5) Reconcile logs from sla-service and routing-engine to see if normalized_timestamp or local_timestamp used twice
logs: 2026-03-01T02:10:00Z sla-service DECAY computed cohort=prod-escalation-test ticket=SUP-xxxx old_priority=1 computed_priority=1 (expected 1->1 or 0.79)
2026-03-01T02:20:15Z routing-engine APPLY_PRIORITY cohort=prod-escalation-test ticket=SUP-xxxx applied_priority=1 source=decay-job
2026-03-01T02:20:30Z sla-service DECAY computed cohort=prod-escalation-test ticket=SUP-xxxx computed_priority=1 (recomputed by pod slasvc-1)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 09:15 - Support (Priya): Noted replication in prod, created a synthetic cohort and observed same no-decay symptom.
2026-03-01 11:00 - SRE (David): Pulled logs and saw two decay computations close together; hypothesis: leader-election race caused two pods to run decay for overlapping ticket ranges.

2026-03-01 13:40 - Platform Eng (Ana Rodriguez): Found commit in template-compiler v2 that changes template creation timezone metadata to 'local_tz' instead of 'utc' (PR referenced). This metadata is consumed by sla-service and may result in double-normalization.
2026-03-02 08:30 - Analytics (Mark Li): Weekly report query shows cohorts created after the template-compiler v2 migration show the highest discrepancy; older templates behave normally.

2026-03-03 15:20 - Hypothesis A: Two contributions combine to produce the symptom: (1) template metadata includes local_tz causing sla-service to apply a timezone shift, (2) leader-election race causes both old and new pods to run decay without de-duplication for a short window, leading to inconsistent window anchors.
2026-03-04 10:10 - Reproduction attempt: Ran decay job in staging with leader election disabled — decay values matched expected half-life. Re-enabled leader election and reproduced failure pattern.

2026-03-04 14:05 - Data dump: Extracted 72h of decay computation traces and grouped by pod_id; found 2.2% of tickets had overlapping computations within the same 10-min window. Overlap correlates strongly with templates created by template-compiler v2.
analysis: - Template metadata change (local_tz instead of utc) introduced in template-compiler v2 causes sla-service to apply an extra timezone normalization in some code paths.
- Leader-election race condition allows short windows where multiple pods may run decay job for the same cohort due to sharding key changes during pod churn.
- Combination results in anchor timestamps drifting and effectively resetting decay counters for affected tickets, appearing as stalled decay.
- DST transitions and manual template migrations exacerbate the mismatch; tickets created exactly in the impacted window have highest failure rate.
- Race only manifests when pods with differing template-parsing code co-exist (rollout partials).
workaround: 1) Temporarily disable template-compiler v2 feature flag for new template creation to stop new templates from carrying local_tz metadata (frontend toggle done 2026-03-02 18:00 UTC).
2) Backfill: Run a one-off decay-correction job that recomputes priority using canonical UTC anchor for cohorts in the impacted time range (job scheduled 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC).
3) Short-term: Increase decay job leader lease timeout to reduce overlaps until a code fix is deployed (config change applied to prod 2026-03-04 04:00 UTC).
next_steps: 1) Patch sla-service to canonicalize template timezone at ingest boundary and ensure idempotent decay computations (owner: David Chen, ETA: 2026-03-08).
2) Add de-duplication guard in decay scheduler keyed by (cohort, window_anchor) with an atomic lease (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-07).
3) Add end-to-end tests covering DST and leader-election churn in the sla-service integration suite (owner: Platform Eng, ETA: 2026-03-15).
4) Update reporting query to exclude or mark cohorts created during migration window until backfill completes (owner: Analytics, ETA: 2026-03-06).
5) Post-mortem and runbook update: Document this class of failure and remediation steps; notify support and on-call rotation (owner: Priya Menon, ETA: 2026-03-10).
comments: Priya Menon (2026-03-01): Initial ticket created after weekly report flagged P1 median age spike. Included synthetic cohort for reproduction.
David Chen (2026-03-01): I see duplicate decay runs in logs. Assigning to myself to triage and gather traces. Linking to INT-223401 which touched scheduler changes.
Ana Rodriguez (2026-03-02): Noted template metadata change in template-compiler v2 (PR referenced). Will coordinate to disable the flag temporarily.
Mark Li (2026-03-03): Analytics QA confirmed cohort discrepancy; will prepare report slices for templates-by-compiler-version.
SRE-Team (2026-03-04): Increased leader lease TTL to 30s in prod as protective measure; monitoring for overlaps.
resolution: Mitigation applied: template v2 flag disabled and leader lease increased. A code patch to canonicalize timezone and add decay job de-duplication is in review (PR referenced). Backfill job scheduled and running. Final verification pending post-deploy metrics.
notes: Potential follow-ups: audit template migrations for similar metadata drift, add template-compiler version to cohort telemetry.
Business impact: moderate — misrouted workload increases oncall fatigue and contaminates operational metrics; no customer-facing outage reported.
